mechanism: SQLAlchemy 1.4 removes Table.count, so all three pre-existing Masakari purge tests fail while counting their post-purge rows
repair_template: replace a removed table-bound aggregate helper with an explicit select-from aggregate while preserving the assertions

semantic_review.a1_failure: On the unchanged Masakari opening-cutoff snapshot, the three pre-existing purge tests pass with SQLAlchemy 1.3.23. With 1.4.11, all three fail exclusively with AttributeError when their result checks call the removed Table.count helper; the maintainer repair restores all three without changing their expected row counts.
semantic_review.reviewer_basis: Reviewed the one-pin source opening diff, the target maintainer's test-code compatibility change rebased without semantic alteration onto the opening-cutoff snapshot, the cutoff tox command, installed-version probes proving SQLAlchemy 1.3.23/1.4.11/1.4.11, patch applicability, and complete three-arm logs. The same three pre-existing purge tests and their row-count assertions run in every arm; only A1 has the normalized removed-method AttributeError. The Python 3.8/tox 3/virtualenv 20 runner, source-era setuptools seed, Cython build constraint, and pip seed are identical across arms and only restore opening-era packaging compatibility.
semantic_review.source_effect: The source opening changes exactly one upper-constraints pin, SQLAlchemy 1.3.23 to 1.4.11; SQLAlchemy 1.4 removes the legacy Table.count convenience method used by the target's result checks.
semantic_review.target_repair: The maintainer change applies to the public opening-cutoff Masakari snapshot and replaces only the removed count invocation with select(func.count()).select_from(table). The same three purge operations and exact row-count assertions remain; no test is deleted, skipped, weakened, or newly introduced.
